ProgramName: Master of Advanced Studies in Climate Science and Policy
Description: The Master of Advanced Studies in Climate Science and Policy (MAS-CSP) is a one-year professional degree that gives students the knowledge they need to become leaders in the field of climate policy. Offered by Scripps Institution of Oceanography, the MAS-CSP curriculum is designed to teach students the fundamentals of climate science, how to evaluate the impacts of climate change, and how to effectively communicate and implement solutions. The program combines coursework from the physical, biological, and social sciences with professional training in communication and policy-making. Graduates of the MAS-CSP program are prepared to pursue careers in a wide array of fields, including government agencies, non-profits, and the private sector.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

ProgramName: Master of Science in Earth Sciences
Description: The Master of Science degree in Earth Sciences is a graduate program offered by the Earth Science program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, in conjunction with the Graduate Division at UC San Diego. The program is designed for students who are interested in a terminal master’s degree with a focus in a specific area of Earth Sciences. The Earth Sciences M.S. degree provides a strong foundation for a variety of career pathways in industry, government, and education, and gives students the tools necessary to tackle a wide range of environmental problems. M.S. students will engage in a rigorous curriculum that includes quantitative coursework and training in computational analysis. The program also requires the completion of a capstone project which can be either a research-based thesis or a literature-based review paper on a topic of the student’s choosing, conducted under the supervision of a faculty advisor. The curriculum is intended to be completed in one year, but can be extended to two years for students with limited prior training in Earth Sciences.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, scholarships, and graduate student researcher (GSR) appointments

Description: The Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans, and Planets (GEO) curricular group at Scripps Institution of Oceanography encompasses a broad range of scientific disciplines focused on the Earth’s physical, chemical, and biological systems, from the deep interior to the oceans and atmosphere. Researchers in GEO study the fundamental processes that govern the evolution of the planet, the causes and consequences of natural hazards like earthquakes and volcanic eruptions, and the dynamics of the Earth’s climate system. The GEO curricular group emphasizes a multidisciplinary approach, combining field observations, laboratory experiments, and computational modeling to address some of the most pressing scientific questions of our time. Students in the GEO curricular group have the opportunity to work with leading experts in their fields, and to conduct research in some of the most remote and challenging environments on Earth. The GEO curricular group is also home to a number of world-class research facilities, including the Cecil H. and Ida M. Green Institute of Geophysics and Planetary Physics (IGPP), the Geosciences Research Division (GRD), and a number of analytical laboratories.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted PhD students receive a financial support package that covers tuition, fees, and an annual stipend ($39,534.84 for 2024-2025).
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) appointments, and/or Teaching Assistant (TA) appointments

ProgramName: PhD in Earth Sciences with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
Requirements: The following materials must be submitted via the online application for an application to be considered complete: Statement of Purpose, Three Letters of Recommendation, Resume or CV, and Transcripts. In the statement of purpose we would like to hear about your previous research experience and your research interests for graduate school. Please be sure to list any SIO faculty members with whom you are interested in working. Applicants are strongly encouraged to communicate with potential advisors before applying. The GRE General Test is not required for Fall 2024 admissions. For international applicants whose native language is not English and who have not studied full-time for at least one uninterrupted academic year at a university-level institution in which English is the language of instruction and in a country in which English is a dominant language, the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) or International English Language Testing System (IELTS) is required.
Description: The Interdisciplinary Environmental Research (PIER) Program is an optional specialization in the PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography. PIER is designed to train a new generation of scientists and leaders to research and solve complex and interdisciplinary environmental problems. The PIER program provides an opportunity for students to specialize in a chosen field of research and to acquire the breadth and skills to work on problems that cross traditional disciplinary boundaries. Students gain this experience through a combination of interdisciplinary courses, seminars and colloquia, and an internship program that places them in a non-academic environment to gain experience in applying their knowledge. Admission to the PIER specialization is a two-step process. First, students must apply and be admitted to the PhD program at Scripps. Once accepted into the Scripps PhD program, students may apply to the PIER program for admission.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Research Assistantships (GSR), Teaching Assistantships (TA)

ProgramName: PhD in Geophysics (Joint with San Diego State University)
Description: The Joint Doctoral Program in Geophysics with San Diego State University (SDSU) is a PhD program that operates under the framework of the existing Scripps Institution of Oceanography PhD program. Students have access to the broad resources of both institutions. In addition to a rigorous training in the fundamentals of geophysics, the program exposes students to a variety of research topics, and provides flexibility in designing a course of study that best suits their interests. Students interested in the Joint Program in Geophysics can apply through either UC San Diego or SDSU. Admission requirements are the same for both institutions and applications are evaluated by a joint admissions committee. Applicants are encouraged to contact potential advisors in their area of interest at either or both institutions.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: All admitted PhD students receive a funding package which includes a monthly stipend ($3,349.50 as of Oct 2023) and payment of all university fees and tuition.
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of admitted students are guaranteed financial support.

ProgramName: Master of Advanced Studies in Marine Biodiversity and Conservation
Requirements: A complete online application includes the following: Online Application and Fee, Statement of Purpose: Describe your academic and professional background, and why you are interested in the MAS MBC program., Resume or CV, Three Letters of Recommendation, Official Transcripts, TOEFL or IELTS Scores (for international applicants only), There is NO GRE requirement for the MAS MBC program.
Description: The Master of Advanced Studies (MAS) degree in Marine Biodiversity and Conservation (MBC) at Scripps Institution of Oceanography at UC San Diego is a 12-month, intensive program that is geared towards resource managers, environmental consultants, and informal science educators. Our goal is to train the next generation of leaders in marine conservation. This is accomplished through a comprehensive curriculum of interdisciplinary coursework and a collaborative, solution-based capstone project. In just one year, our students receive a broad introduction to the science, economics, and policy of marine conservation and gain practical skills to improve their effectiveness in the environmental arena.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Need-based scholarships, Paid student researcher positions

ProgramName: Master of Science in Marine Biology
Description: The master of science (M.S.) in marine biology is a two-year course of study that provides a broad, interdisciplinary education in marine biology. The M.S. degree is earned by the satisfactory completion of a minimum of 36 units of graduate coursework and the successful completion of a capstone requirement. The M.S. is considered a terminal degree at Scripps Institution of Oceanography, and students admitted to the M.S. program will not be able to transfer to the Ph.D. program. The marine biology M.S. degree is a Plan II (non-thesis) degree. The capstone requirement will consist of either: 1) a literature-based capstone paper and its defense at an oral examination, or 2) passing the Ph.D. departmental exam. Both options require an extensive literature review that demonstrates mastery of a specific area of marine biology. The capstone project must be completed by the end of the student’s second year of study.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Description: The Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in marine biology science. Research in the Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps is managed through three multi-disciplinary research sections: Integrative Oceanography Division (IOD), Marine Biology Research Division (MBRD), and Center for Marine Biotechnology and Biomedicine (CMBB). Students are admitted into the PhD program and receive their degree through the Scripps Oceanography department. Marine Biology students are part of a unique department that houses a large diversity of scientific disciplines that all have in common a focus on the oceans. This allows for a truly interdisciplinary educational experience for our students. In addition to a broad suite of graduate courses in marine biology, students have access to courses in the other curricular programs at Scripps (Climate-Ocean-Atmosphere; Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans, and Planets; Ocean Biosciences) and in other departments at UC San Diego (e.g., Division of Biological Sciences, School of Medicine, Skaggs School of Pharmacy).
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: Full tuition and fees plus a stipend (2023-2024 nine-month GSR salary is $37,000)
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) appointments, and Teaching Assistant (TA) appointments

ProgramName: PhD in Marine Biology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
Description: The Marine Biology PhD program at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in marine biology and biological oceanography. Students are encouraged to develop their own research program from a wide range of fields including ecology, physiology, molecular biology, and symbiosis, applied to a diverse array of ocean ecosystems and organisms, ranging from microbes to whales. Marine Biology PhD students are based in two research sections at Scripps, Marine Biology Research Division (MBRD) and Integrative Oceanography Division (IOD). The core of the PhD curriculum is an interdisciplinary education in ocean sciences along with in-depth knowledge in marine biology and biological oceanography, and professional training in science communication, grant writing, teaching, and leadership. Students also have the option of pursuing a PhD specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research. This specialization is for students interested in an interdisciplinary approach to research on environmental problems. Graduate students affiliated with PIER gain a broader perspective and a specialized skillset to tackle the world’s most challenging environmental problems.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: Up to $32,000 stipend plus tuition and fees

Description: The Master of Science in Oceanography at Scripps Institution of Oceanography is a terminal Master’s degree intended for students who have a strong science background and wish to get interdisciplinary training in oceanography. This degree provides students with knowledge of the diverse sub-disciplines of oceanography and the tools to succeed in a variety of related careers in industry, government, or education. The program takes between one to two years to complete. Students are required to take 36 units and complete a capstone project. Students work with a faculty advisor and a capstone committee to design and complete their project.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Requirements: Scripps Institution of Oceanography (SIO) seeks to admit a diverse and outstanding student body. Students are selected based on their scholastic record and potential for success in graduate school. No single factor is used to make admission decisions. The department considers all application materials, including statement of purpose, letters of recommendation, resume/CV, and academic preparation (coursework and research experience).

Description: The PhD in Oceanography degree program is an advanced, research-based degree that requires the completion of a dissertation of publishable quality that makes an original and significant contribution to oceanography. The program is organized into three separate Curricular Groups: Climate-Ocean-Atmosphere Program (COAP), Geosciences of the Earth, Oceans and Planets (GEO), and Ocean Biosciences Program (OBP). Students enroll in one of the three Curricular Groups based upon their research interests.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Guaranteed financial support through external fellowships, internal fellowships, graduate student researcherships (GSR), and/or teaching assistantships (TA).

ProgramName: PhD in Oceanography with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
Requirements: A Statement of Purpose is required. Please use the statement to address the following: What is your motivation to pursue a graduate degree in ocean, earth, or climate science?; How do your research interests align with research being conducted at Scripps?; What are your research goals and how would a degree from Scripps help you achieve them?; How have you prepared for graduate school? What skills and knowledge have you gained from your previous academic, research, professional, and/or personal experiences? What challenges have you faced and how did you overcome them?; What are your personal and professional goals after completing a graduate degree? We encourage you to review the UC San Diego Graduate Division’s guidance on writing a statement of purpose. A Resume or CV is required. Three Letters of Recommendation are required. Transcripts are required from all post-secondary institutions attended. Both a scanned unofficial copy and an official copy are required by the admissions deadline. International applicants may be required to submit scores from the TOEFL iBT or IELTS. The minimum TOEFL score required for consideration for admission is 550 for the paper-based test, 213 for the computer-based test, or 80 for the internet-based test. The minimum required IELTS score is 7.
Description: The Interdisciplinary Environmental Research (PIER) PhD specialization is designed to allow students to pursue interdisciplinary environmental research and to provide them with the background necessary to be leaders in the field of environmental research. Students admitted to the PIER specialization pursue research and coursework that is truly interdisciplinary, spanning the natural and social sciences. Students are expected to define and pursue a program of study and research that includes two or more of the traditional disciplines. Students in the PIER specialization are expected to fulfill all of the curricular requirements of their home PhD program plus PIER-specific requirements.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: Guaranteed financial support for up to five years, which includes full payment of tuition and fees, plus an annual stipend of $40,000 (2023-24 rate).
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of tuition and fees
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Graduate Student Research position (GSR), Teaching Assistantship (TA)

Description: The doctoral program in Anthropology at UC San Diego is one of the top programs in the country. We are ranked 6th in the nation in the most recent National Research Council (NRC) rankings of graduate programs. We are also ranked among the top programs by other measures, such as the number of federal grants received by our graduate students for their dissertation research. The department’s distinguished faculty is one of the most outstanding in the country in terms of its scholarly productivity and its success in training graduate students. We have a distinct profile in American anthropology due to the strong integration of its subfields—archaeological, biological, sociocultural, and linguistic anthropology—and its close ties with other disciplines, interdisciplinary programs and research centers across the campus. We admit a small, select group of students each year. This allows for close intellectual engagement between faculty and students.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of tuition and fees for the first five years

ProgramName: PhD in Anthropology and Cognitive Science
Description: The Department of Anthropology and the interdisciplinary Cognitive Science Program offer an interdisciplinary Ph.D. in Anthropology and Cognitive Science. The program provides a unique course of study for students with interests in both Anthropology and Cognitive Science. Students in the program receive a solid grounding in both fields, and do research that is jointly supervised by faculty from both departments. Students apply through and are admitted into the Anthropology department. For information about the Cognitive Science program and faculty, please visit the Cognitive Science website.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcherships (GSR), Teaching Assistantships (TA)

Description: The Anthropological track of the Science Studies Program focuses on the ethnographic study of science, technology, and medicine. Anthropological science studies scholars analyze scientific and technical work where it happens -- in laboratories, clinics, and field sites -- as well as in the social worlds where scientific knowledge and technologies circulate. Anthropologists of science, technology, and medicine pay close attention to the ways in which local and global relations of power shape and are shaped by technoscience. The track brings these ethnographic sensibilities to the interdisciplinary field of science studies. Our faculty's expertise is global in scope, with particular strengths in Latin America, the United States, and Asia. Faculty and graduate students in the track are affiliated with a number of interdisciplinary programs on campus, including the Institute for Practical Ethics, the Center for Global Health, and Critical Gender Studies.

ProgramName: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny
Description:
The Anthropology Department, in collaboration with the Center for Academic Research and Training in Anthropogeny (CARTA) and the Salk Institute for Biological studies, offers a PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Anthropogeny. This specialization is designed to train graduate students in the transdisciplinary field of anthropogeny. Anthropogeny investigates the origin of humans. This is a vast and complex topic, requiring the integration of multiple disciplines from the social, behavioral, biomedical, and biological sciences.
The primary goals of this specialization are: To help students develop the ability to communicate across the different disciplines that contribute to anthropogeny. To provide a foundation of knowledge across these disciplines. To foster the transdisciplinary way of thinking that is necessary to fully explore the origin of humans.
Students will: Attend a three-quarter course sequence in anthropogeny. Participate in a quarterly CARTA-sponsored symposia series. Be eligible to receive fellowship support.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

ProgramName: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Cognitive Science
Requirements: The UCSD Application for Graduate Admission is online. Applications are accepted for the PhD program for Fall quarter admission only. Applicants may apply to both the PhD program in Anthropology and the MAS program in the Anthropology of Climate Change. A separate application and fee are required for each program. Please review the Anthropology Graduate Admissions FAQs before applying. Required application materials for the PhD program include: the online application with application fee; statement of purpose; three letters of recommendation; a resume or curriculum vitae; a writing sample; transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended; and TOEFL or IELTS scores for international applicants. The Department of Anthropology does not require GRE scores. For more detailed information on graduate admissions in Anthropology, visit the department website.
Description:
The Department of Anthropology, in conjunction with the Interdisciplinary PhD Program in Cognitive Science, offers a specialization in cognitive science for students in sociocultural, psychological, or biological anthropology. Anthropology is the study of human beings in the widest possible sense. It is a discipline that is global in its scope, historical in its depth, and holistic in its approach. Cognitive science is the interdisciplinary study of intelligent systems, both natural and artificial. It draws from anthropology, computer science, linguistics, neuroscience, philosophy, and psychology. The specialization in cognitive science is intended to provide anthropology students with a deeper understanding of the theories and methods of this allied discipline and to allow them to pursue research that crosses the boundaries between the two fields.

At the core of the specialization are two year-long proseminar courses that introduce students to the essential concepts and methods of cognitive science and a practicum in which students gain hands-on experience in the laboratory of a cognitive science faculty member. Additional advanced courses are available on a wide variety of topics. Students who complete the specialization will receive a parenthetical on their diploma: “PhD in Anthropology (with a Specialization in Cognitive Science).”
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) positions, Teaching Assistant (TA) positions

ProgramName: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Computational Social Science
Requirements: Please be sure to submit all of the required application materials. This will ensure your application is reviewed in a timely manner. The following is a list of all required materials: Transcripts, Resume or Curriculum Vitae, Letters of Recommendation, Statement of Purpose, English Language Proficiency, Writing Sample(s)
Description: The Department of Anthropology at UC San Diego is committed to the four-field approach, integrating sociocultural anthropology, biological anthropology, psychological anthropology, and anthropological archaeology. We also have a strong focus on the anthropological study of language and communication. The Ph.D. program is designed to provide the theoretical background and methodological skills necessary for a career in professional research and teaching in anthropology. The department has a strong focus on the anthropology of the Americas and the Pacific Rim.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowship, Teaching Assistantship (TA), Graduate Student Researcher (GSR)

ProgramName: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Critical Gender Studies
Requirements:
In addition to the general requirements for admission to graduate studies at UCSD, the following materials must be submitted online by the deadline for your application to be considered:

In your statement you should address the following: What specific research questions or problems in anthropology are you interested in pursuing? In which of the department's three subfields (archaeological, biological, or sociocultural anthropology) does your research interest lie? Which faculty members in the department are you most interested in working with and why? What previous experiences have prepared you for graduate study in anthropology?
2. Three Letters of Recommendation: Enter the names and contact information of your recommenders in the online application. Recommenders will be contacted by email and will be asked to submit their letters electronically.
3. Transcripts: Upload a copy of transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended.

We recommend submitting a single-authored piece that highlights your abilities to write and reason anthropologically. There is no specific page length required, but we suggest a writing sample around 20 pages.
5. Resume or C.V.

7. TOEFL or IELTS: Required for international applicants whose native language is not English and who have not studied full-time for one uninterrupted academic year at a university-level institution in which English is the language of instruction and in a country in which English is a dominant language.
Description: Our doctoral program in Anthropology offers a rigorous training in the four sub-fields of the discipline: sociocultural, biological, and archaeological anthropology and anthropological linguistics. Although students are admitted to a specific sub-field, they are expected to gain a broad understanding of the whole discipline and to develop a research project of their own that may draw upon more than one sub-field. The first two years are spent in coursework, at the end of which students must pass a foreign language exam and write a second-year paper. After advancing to candidacy, by passing a qualifying exam, students carry out a major piece of independent fieldwork. The final stage of the program is the writing of a doctoral dissertation. While the department offers a focus in each of the four main sub-fields of anthropology, it is well known for a number of specializations that cut across these. These include: psychological anthropology, medical anthropology, the anthropology of modernity, the anthropology of religion, political anthropology, the anthropology of climate change, human-animal-environmental interactions, and the study of language in society.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, research grants, and teaching assistantships

ProgramName: PhD in Anthropology with a Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research
Description: The Department of Anthropology at UC San Diego offers a program of graduate studies leading to the PhD degree. The Department has a distinctive profile within the discipline of anthropology. We are well-known as a department that is theoretically innovative and that bridges the traditional sub-fields of the discipline through an interdisciplinary and contemporary focus. We are committed to a comparative and critical understanding of what it is to be human in a complex and changing world. Our graduate curriculum reflects our department’s intellectual profile and commitment to holistic and integrated anthropology for the 21st century. The PhD program offers two specializations: Anthropogeny and Interdisciplinary Environmental Research. The Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research is designed for doctoral students who wish to communicate and collaborate with researchers across a wide range of academic disciplines in the natural sciences, physical sciences, social sciences, and humanities that are pursuing environmentally-focused research. The graduate Specialization in Interdisciplinary Environmental Research is a PhD specialization that may be taken in conjunction with any of the PhD degree programs at UC San Diego.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR), and Teaching Assistant (TA) positions

Description: The Astrophysics Ph.D. is an interdisciplinary program that includes researchers from the Department of Physics and the Center for Astrophysics and Space Sciences (CASS). CASS is one of the largest and most vibrant astrophysics groups in the world, with a broad range of research interests, including cosmology, galaxy formation, high-energy astrophysics, and exoplanets. Our astrophysics program emphasizes a broad education in fundamental physics as well as a focus on cutting edge research. Students are encouraged to get involved in research during their first year. Research at UC San Diego spans the full range of observational and theoretical astrophysics. We have a diverse faculty that actively participate in student mentorship. UC San Diego is a major partner in the Lick and Keck observatories, which ensures our students and faculty have guaranteed access to world-class facilities. We encourage you to browse our faculty page for more information on the research being carried out at UC San Diego. Our graduate students are also encouraged to interact with the broader San Diego astronomy community through events like the San Diego Astronomy Journal Club (SDAJC). For more information, please visit our prospective students page or attend one of our info sessions.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships (TA), Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) appointments

ProgramName: Doctor of Audiology (AuD) (Joint with San Diego State University)
Requirements: A bachelor's degree (or equivalent) is required for admission to the AuD program. An undergraduate major in speech, language, and hearing sciences is not required; students from other disciplines are encouraged to apply, but they must complete the specified prerequisites prior to entry into the graduate program. A minimum GPA of 3.0 is required for admission, but the program is very competitive and the mean GPA of admitted students is approximately 3.7. Prerequisites: Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Hearing (or separate courses in Anatomy and Physiology of Speech and Anatomy and Physiology of Hearing), Phonetics, Language Acquisition, Introduction to Audiology, Aural Rehabilitation, Speech and Hearing Science, and one course in physical sciences (e.g., physics or chemistry), one course in biological sciences, one course in social sciences, and one course in statistics.
Department: Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science
Description: The Doctor of Audiology (Au.D.) is a professional degree that replaced the master’s degree as the entry-level degree for audiologists. The joint Au.D. program between San Diego State University and the University of California, San Diego provides students with a strong scientific and theoretical foundation in hearing and balance sciences and disorders, as well as extensive and varied clinical experiences. The program is designed to train audiologists to be leaders in the field and to provide the highest quality, evidence-based services to their patients. Graduates of our program are employed in a wide variety of clinical settings (e.g., hospitals, private practices, ENT offices), industry, and educational and research settings.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
Accredidation: The Doctoral Program (Au.D.) in Audiology at San Diego State University and University of California, San Diego is accredited by the Council on Academic Accreditation in Audiology and Speech-Language Pathology (CAA) of the American Speech-Language-Hearing Association, 2200 Research Boulevard #310, Rockville, Maryland 20850, 800-498-2071 or 301-296-5700.

A resume or curriculum vitae is required. Transcripts are required. Please upload a copy of your transcripts to the online application. This can be an unofficial copy.
Description: The Department of Bioengineering offers a Master of Science (M.S.) degree in Bioengineering. The M.S. program is designed to provide a deeper level of education than is possible in the B.S. program, but not the extensive research and specialization of the doctoral program. For this reason, the M.S. program may be a desirable terminal degree for students who plan to seek industrial employment or it may be a desirable intermediate degree for students who wish to enter the doctoral program at a later date. Both a thesis and a non-thesis option are available for the M.S. program. For both options, all M.S. students must successfully complete a set of core courses. This requirement is intended to provide a broad, graduate-level background in physiology, tissue engineering, and biomechanics. Beyond these core courses, M.S. students are encouraged to specialize by selecting a sequence of courses in their area of interest.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipPercentage: up to 25%
ScholarshipType: Departmental fellowships, Partial fee scholarships, Teaching Assistantships, Readerships

Description: The Ph.D. program is designed to provide students with the background, training, and original research experience to become successful independent investigators in academia or industry. The focus of the program is on the integration of principles and applications from engineering, biology, and medicine. The Ph.D. program is research-oriented and requires the completion of an independent research project and a dissertation. The program culminates in the Ph.D. in Bioengineering degree. This requires completion of at least 48 units of coursework, research, and seminar, passing a departmental qualifying examination, and defending a dissertation that describes the results of original and independent research.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Graduate Student Research positions

ProgramName: Master of Science in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology
Requirements: A bachelor's degree in a scientific or engineering discipline with a strong quantitative and analytical background, and at least one year of Biology, one year of Chemistry, one year of Physics and one year of Mathematics including calculus and statistics. Linear algebra and programming experience is highly recommended. The most competitive applicants typically have extensive laboratory and/or programming experience.
Description: The goal of the MS in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology is to train the next generation of scientists who are able to analyze large-scale biological and clinical data sets and to develop novel computational and mathematical approaches to solve pressing problems in biology and medicine. This MS program provides a rigorous, interdisciplinary training that combines coursework in biology, computer science, mathematics, statistics, and bioinformatics, with a thesis research project that will allow students to gain hands-on experience in cutting-edge research. The program prepares students for positions in the biotechnology and pharmaceutical industries as well as for entry into Ph.D. programs in bioinformatics and other related fields. The Bioinformatics and Systems Biology (BISB) MS degree program requires a minimum of forty-eight units of coursework, research, and a written thesis. The MS program takes approximately two years to complete, with a maximum time limit of three years.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

ProgramName: PhD in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology

A satisfactory scholastic average, usually a minimum grade-point average (GPA) of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required. Please see the Graduate Division's pages on minimum admissions requirements for US applicants and international applicants for more information.
Description: The Ph.D. in Bioinformatics and Systems Biology is an interdisciplinary program that brings together faculty from the Division of Biological Sciences, the School of Medicine, the Jacobs School of Engineering (Departments of Bioengineering, Computer Science and Engineering), and the Physical Sciences Division (Departments of Chemistry & Biochemistry and Mathematics). The interdisciplinary nature of the program is ideal for students with undergraduate degrees in a wide range of fields, including biology, biochemistry, chemistry, computer science, mathematics, and bioengineering. The program aims to train the next generation of scientists who can bridge the fields of biology, medicine, and computer science and engineering; as such, we offer a rigorous and flexible curriculum that can be tailored to an individual student's interests. The program is committed to a culture of collaboration with students at the very core of our program. Students are mentored by top-tier faculty who are experts in their fields, and have the opportunity to participate in a variety of research areas.

Our program is interdisciplinary and features research in seven main areas: Cell Biology, Development & Genetics; Ecology, Behavior & Evolution; Molecular Biology; Neurobiology; Plant Biology; Quantitative Biology & Bioinformatics; and Microbiology. The program is built on a foundation of cutting-edge research and a curriculum of challenging and exciting courses that lead to a Ph.D. in Biology. The Ph.D. Program is a full-time, year-round program that trains students for careers as research scientists and educators.

The degree may be a terminal degree or obtained in the course of a PhD program. The graduate program also offers a combined BA/MS degree program for undergraduate students at UC San Diego. The program involves didactic courses and an independent research project performed under the supervision of a faculty member. The MS degree requires an oral defense of the thesis or a comprehensive exam. Both plans require a minimum of 36 units.

Students will receive training in the classroom and in the laboratory in a wide range of topics that span the continuum from basic to translational “bench to bedside” research. All BMS students are provided with a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of biomedical sciences through both didactic course work and laboratory research. The program offers tracks and specializations that allow students to obtain more in-depth training in specific areas including Bioinformatics, Anthropogeny, and the Medical Scientist Training Program (MSTP).

Department: Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science
Description: The Master of Science in Biostatistics is an exclusively-designed program of the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science that aims to train the next generation of biostatisticians who will have a strong quantitative background, an understanding of the biological mechanisms of disease, and the ability to apply statistical methods to solve problems in public health and biomedical sciences. Our graduate students are provided with rigorous classroom instruction and hands-on data analysis experiences that prepare them for careers in academia, industry, and government. The curriculum is designed to be completed in six quarters, although it is possible for some students to complete the program in less time. For more information regarding our program including course requirements, please visit the UC San Diego Course Catalog and the program's Student Handbook.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Department: Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science
Description: The Ph.D. in Biostatistics is an interdepartmental program offered by the Division of Biostatistics in the Herbert Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science and the Halicioglu Data Science Institute, in affiliation with the Department of Mathematics. The program is designed to train independent researchers in biostatistical theory and methodology. Graduates of the program are prepared for careers in academia, industry and government. The program requires a dissertation. Students in this program will learn to build a strong foundation in statistical theory and methods. They will learn to apply statistical methods to the design of experimental and observational studies in the health sciences and to the analysis of data from such studies. Students will also gain the skills to extend existing statistical methods and to develop new ones for applications in the health sciences. The program emphasizes the important role of computing in modern statistics and ensures that students become proficient with a number of statistical software packages. Finally, through required coursework as well as seminars and research collaborations with faculty, students will learn to effectively communicate the results of their statistical analyses to both technical and non-technical audiences.

The program offers a rigorous, hands-on training that will prepare you to use data and analytics to identify business opportunities, generate business insights and create business solutions. As an MSBA student, you will gain the quantitative skills to create and manage business analytics and the business acumen to lead data-driven decision making.

Description: The M.A. degree is intended for students who want a broader-based master’s degree. Students who wish to enroll in the M.A. degree program must be admitted to the department’s Ph.D. program. There is no direct admission to the M.A. program. After completion of one year of study in the Ph.D. program, students may petition to change from the Ph.D. program to the M.A. program. The M.A. is a non-thesis degree and requires the completion of 36 units of course work. At least 24 of these units must be in chemistry, and at least 12 of the 24 units must be in graduate-level chemistry lecture courses. The remaining 12 units can be in any graduate-level science, math or engineering courses, or in upper division undergraduate courses in these fields with consent of the vice chair for the graduate education committee. In addition, the student must have a B average in the course work. All M.A. degree requirements must be completed within two years. M.A. candidates are not eligible for any financial support from the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Description:
The M.S. degree is offered with a major in chemistry. It is not required as a prerequisite for the Ph.D. degree. The M.S. degree in chemistry may be taken with one of three plans:
Plan I (Thesis): A minimum of 36 units of credit is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level courses. The remaining 12 units must be in upper-division (100-level) or graduate-level courses. A maximum of 12 of the 36 required units may be taken for a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory grade. At least 12 of the 36 units must be in chemistry research (CHEM 299). A thesis is required. The thesis must be approved by a committee of three faculty members, and the student must pass an oral examination on the thesis research.
Plan II (Comprehensive Examination): A minimum of 36 units of credit is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level courses. The remaining 12 units must be in upper-division (100-level) or graduate-level courses. A maximum of 8 of the 36 required units may be taken for a Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory grade. No more than 4 of these units can be in non-letter graded research, CHEM 297 or CHEM 299. Satisfactory performance on a comprehensive examination is required.
Plan IV (Coursework): A minimum of 48 units of credit in upper-division (100-level) and graduate-level courses is required. At least 24 of these units must be in graduate-level chemistry courses, excluding special study (CHEM 296, 297, 299). A maximum of 8 units of upper-division courses may be taken in a related field. No units of research (CHEM 299) may be included in the 48 units of credit. Satisfactory performance on a comprehensive examination is required.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Description: The Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry offers a program of graduate study leading to the Doctor of Philosophy. The PhD program is designed to develop students into scientists who are experts in their chosen area of research. These areas include Analytical, Atmospheric, Biochemistry, Biophysics, Chemical Biology, Inorganic, Nanoscience, Organic, Physical, and Theoretical Chemistry. The program provides the broad chemical background required to support this development as well as opportunities for students to develop skills as teachers and mentors.

ProgramName: PhD in Clinical Psychology (Joint with San Diego State University)
Requirements:
Successful applicants to the Joint Doctoral Program in Clinical Psychology generally possess the following qualifications:
1. An undergraduate major in psychology, or at least 30 undergraduate semester hours in psychology.
2. A grade point average of 3.5 or better in all psychology courses, and an overall undergraduate GPA of 3.5 or better.
3. Completion of a course in statistics (preferably in psychology, but other social/behavioral sciences are acceptable) and a course in research methods. Additional coursework in the biological and physical sciences is also desirable.
4. Research experience, typically one to two years in a faculty member's lab.
5. Strong letters of recommendation, including at least two from faculty who can speak to the applicant's research potential and academic skills.
6. A well-written personal statement describing the applicant's research interests and career goals, including the identification of one or two JDP faculty with whom they would like to work.
Concentration: Behavioral Medicine, Experimental Psychopathology, and Neuropsychology
Description: The SDSU/UC San Diego Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Clinical Psychology is one of the nation's outstanding clinical psychology doctoral programs. The program has been continuously accredited by the American Psychological Association since 1989. The program's mission is to train clinical psychologists who are well-grounded in the science of psychology and who will be able to apply their scientific knowledge and methods to the advancement of human welfare. The program faculty have a wide range of interests which is reflected in the three major areas of study offered in the program: Behavioral Medicine, Experimental Psychopathology, and Neuropsychology. The program is committed to fostering diversity among its faculty and students.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
Accredidation: The program has been continuously accredited by the American Psychological Association since 1989.

Requirements: All applicants must have a bachelor's degree or the equivalent from an accredited institution in the United States or from a recognized university-level academic institution abroad. A grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 or better, or the equivalent, is required by the Graduate Division. The department may consider exceptions. The Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) is required for international applicants whose native language is not English. Minimum TOEFL score is 550 on the paper-based test (pBT), 213 on the computer-based test (cBT), and 85 on the internet-based test (iBT). Applicants who have received a degree from a university in which English is the language of instruction may be exempt from the TOEFL requirement.
Description: The Department of Communication at UC San Diego offers a doctoral program that is distinctive in its dual focus on communication as a social and a cultural practice, and on the central role of communication and media technologies in shaping and transforming these practices. We are committed to a critical and empirical approach to the study of communication. The program is interdisciplinary in its orientation, drawing on faculty and curricula in the humanities, social sciences and to a lesser extent, in the fine arts and engineering. We offer a single, integrated PhD program in Communication, one in which students must work across at least two of the department’s three main areas of research.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Description: The Science Studies Program at UC San Diego is a joint doctoral program of the Departments of Communication, History, Philosophy, and Sociology. It is the oldest and one of the most respected programs of its kind in the world. The program offers interdisciplinary training for students to study the historical and contemporary connections among the sciences, social sciences, humanities, technology, and medicine. Core requirements include a two-quarter Core Seminar and a one-quarter seminar on contemporary science, technology, and medicine studies. Elective seminars from the four participating departments provide the primary course work for students. The Departments of Communication, History, Philosophy, and Sociology each admit students into the Science Studies Program. Applicants should specify which of the four departments they wish to apply to on the university’s application form.

The curriculum is a mixture of courses and a research project or thesis intended to provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary for a professional career or to continue to a doctoral program. Our students in the M.S. program have gone on to be very successful in industry at major companies such as Google and Microsoft as well as startups. The M.S. can also be an excellent stepping stone for a Ph.D. program. Many of our M.S. students go on to be admitted into Ph.D. programs either here at UCSD or at another top university. The M.S. program is very competitive. We receive well over 3,000 applications each year.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Computer Science with a Specialization in Human-Centered Design
Description: The M.S. in Computer Science with a Specialization in Human-Centered Design (HCD) prepares students to be leaders in the research and design of next-generation human-computer interactions. The program is a collaboration between the Departments of Computer Science and Engineering (CSE), Cognitive Science (Cogs), and Communication (Comm). Students will take classes in all three departments, learning the theories, methods, and principles needed to design, implement, and evaluate technology from a human-centered perspective. The HCD specialization prepares students for careers as user experience (UX) researchers, interaction designers, usability engineers, and software developers at companies across the globe. Students are required to take five core classes, as well as a selection of electives, and can complete the degree by thesis or comprehensive exam.

Human-Centered Design is a creative, problem-solving process that seeks to create technology that is useful, usable, and desirable. The specialization includes courses and research opportunities with faculty in CSE and other departments. The program offers a unique opportunity to conduct research in Human-Centered Design in the context of a world-class engineering department and university.

Students who pursue the specialization in Computer Engineering will gain a deep understanding of the principles of computer design and implementation, as well as the ability to apply these principles to solve real-world problems. Description: The Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering with a Specialization in Bioinformatics is an interdisciplinary program between the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the Bioinformatics and Systems Biology Interdepartmental Program. The program is for students who wish to pursue a Ph.D. in Computer Science and Engineering and are interested in research that bridges the fields of computer science and life sciences. All students in this program are required to complete a series of courses in computer science, bioinformatics and life sciences as well as conduct thesis research at the interface of these fields. This program is administered by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering. Students wishing to apply to this program must submit an application for the Computer Science and Engineering Ph.D. program (Program Code CS76) and select the Bioinformatics Specialization on the application.

ProgramName: Master of Advanced Studies in Data Science and Engineering
Description: The Master of Advanced Study (MAS) in Data Science and Engineering is designed to meet the needs of working professionals who want to develop deep expertise in data science and engineering to advance their careers. The MAS in Data Science and Engineering provides a rigorous, hands-on curriculum that encompasses both the principles of data science and the engineering skills needed to build and deploy large-scale data systems. Students will learn the latest techniques in machine learning, statistics, and data mining, as well as the fundamentals of data systems, including databases, distributed computing, and data visualization. The program culminates in a capstone project in which students work in teams to solve a real-world data science problem. The MAS in Data Science and Engineering is a part-time, self-supporting program that can be completed in two years. Courses are offered in the evenings and on weekends to accommodate the schedules of working professionals. Students will have the opportunity to interact with leading researchers and practitioners in data science and engineering, and to network with other professionals in the field. The program is offered jointly by the Department of Computer Science and Engineering and the San Diego Supercomputer Center. Students will have access to the state-of-the-art computing resources of the San Diego Supercomputer Center, and will have the opportunity to work with real-world datasets from a variety of domains. The program prepares students for careers as data scientists, data engineers, and data analysts in a wide range of industries, including technology, finance, healthcare, and e-commerce. Graduates will be equipped with the skills and knowledge to design, build, and deploy data-driven solutions to the challenges of Big Data.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering (Advanced Manufacturing)
Description:
The Master of Science in Electrical and Computer Engineering (Advanced Manufacturing) program is a specialized professional master's degree program that prepares students for careers in this rapidly growing and dynamic field. Advanced manufacturing is an emerging field that requires significant interdisciplinary engineering training. The program is designed to attract and produce highly skilled engineers who are motivated to be the future leaders in the industry. It builds on the existing academic excellence of the UC San Diego Jacobs School of Engineering, and its close ties with the local and global manufacturing industry, and is a unique addition to the portfolio of engineering disciplines at UC San Diego.

The goal of this innovative program is to produce forward-thinking engineers who will be able to design, build, and manage the advanced manufacturing systems of tomorrow. These systems will rely on sophisticated automation and integrated information technologies that blur the line between bits and atoms. Students in the program will study at the intersection of information technologies, intelligent systems, sensing and control, and manufacturing practices. The curriculum includes four core courses that cover all aspects of advanced manufacturing: design, processes, automation, and supply chains. In addition, students have several technical electives to choose from to build technical depth in their areas of interest, such as additive manufacturing, advanced materials, robotics and automation, and supply chain management. The M.S. program also includes an invaluable internship with a local or global manufacturing company that will give students real-world experience.

A key objective of our program is to equip students with practical skills and state-of-the-art knowledge, with which to be successful as an economist or data analyst in the private or public sector. To this end, our program focuses on topics such as econometrics, applied microeconomics, and computation for economics and big data. Students will develop skills in data analysis and econometric modeling as well as learning to use state-of-the-art statistical software, such as Matlab, Stata, and R. We are a designated STEM program (CIP Code 45.0603: Econometrics and Quantitative Economics). Students with F-1 visas are eligible to apply for a 24-month STEM optional practical training (OPT) extension.

Description: The Ph.D. program in Economics at UC San Diego is a 5-year program designed to train students to be professional economists. The department looks to admit 25-30 students per year. Our graduates have been very successful in securing excellent jobs. You can see a list of our initial placements for the last few years. The first year of the program is devoted to core classes in Macroeconomics, Microeconomics, and Econometrics. These classes provide the basic tools for all economists. At the end of the first year, students take qualifying exams in each of these three areas. In the second and third years, students take field courses to gain expertise in a smaller number of areas. A list of our fields can be found here. Starting in the summer after the first year, students will start working on their own research. The second year paper is due at the start of the third year. This is typically a student's first research paper and is a major requirement for the program. The third year paper is due at the start of the fourth year. This paper is also a major requirement for the program. The fourth and fifth years of the program are devoted to research for the dissertation. The final job market paper is presented at the beginning of the fall quarter of the student's fifth year.

We admit a diverse group of students into a small cohort who work closely with faculty in a supportive and collaborative environment throughout their two years in the program. Students develop a strong foundation in educational theory and practice through a combination of coursework and fieldwork placements in local K-12 schools. Our unique program design allows students to apply what they learn in their university courses in their fieldwork classrooms right away. Description: The Ph.D. in Education: Transforming Education in a Diverse Society is offered as a department-based Ph.D. in Education Studies at UC San Diego. Students in this program are committed to understanding and addressing the educational challenges that face a diverse society. The program of study is interdisciplinary. It draws upon the social sciences, including anthropology, economics, history, political science, psychology and sociology. It is also informed by work in cognitive science, critical theory, cultural studies, discourse analysis, ethnic studies, language and linguistics, and sociolinguistics. The Ph.D. in Education prepares students to conduct research on the pressing educational issues of our time, and to bridge research and practice. In our program, you will develop the knowledge and skills necessary for a career in academia, in educational research, or in other leadership positions. All Ph.D. students specialize in one of three areas. They also must develop an interdisciplinary cognate by taking a series of courses outside of EDS.

Students are trained by faculty artists and scholars with a wealth of experience in the professional world and in academia. The program offers a demanding and intensive journey of artistic exploration and development for a select group of students, with emphasis on individual growth and the creation of a strong ensemble. It culminates with a professional residency in the final quarter of the program, at La Jolla Playhouse. The training nurtures a well-rounded artist who will be prepared for a career in the professional theatre world, in a variety of performance mediums. UC San Diego is a NAST accredited program.

Description: The MFA in Dance is a three-year program that offers graduate students the opportunity to concentrate on choreography and/or performance of contemporary dance. The curriculum supports the development of a strong personal artistic voice and an understanding of the artist's role in society. Courses in choreography, dance technique, performance, teaching, and dance studies are required. Students are provided with regular opportunities to create and show their work, and perform in faculty and student choreographed concerts. The program concludes with a final creative project, which can be a thesis performance of original choreography and/or a performance of a major role. Graduate students have the opportunity to serve as a Teaching Assistant, teaching classes in dance technique, dance studies and/or introductory courses for non-majors. This experience provides essential training for a career in academia.

Requirements: To apply to the Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Design) program, applicants must complete the UC San Diego Online Application for Graduate Admission. Description:
The MFA Design Program at UC San Diego is a three-year program for students who intend to pursue a career as a professional designer in theatre, dance, or other live performance genres. The design program provides an environment where design faculty and students form a community of artists who work together and share a passion for the creation of new works. The program's proximity to a major theatre city allows for regular interaction with professional artists and theatres, which helps to foster an understanding of the current demands of the profession.

The curriculum is flexible and individually tailored, combining rigorous training with an emphasis on new work and new technology. Practical production work is an integral part of the graduate design training program, with each student designing in all four areas (costume, lighting, scenic, sound) for fully-mounted productions in the department's season. In addition, students will have the opportunity to serve as an assistant to a faculty or guest designer.

All graduate students have opportunities to collaborate on projects with MFA directors and playwrights, as well as with students from the PhD program in Theatre and Drama, a joint program with UC Irvine. Design students also collaborate with choreographers in the dance program.

ProgramName: Master of Fine Arts in Theatre and Dance (Directing)
Description:
The three-year Directing program at UC San Diego is a selective and rigorous program dedicated to the artistic, intellectual and professional development of the emerging stage director.

Through a combination of seminars, studio classes, and a robust production season, directors will develop their individual voice and aesthetic while acquiring the necessary skills to lead a creative team through the process of making theatre.

Directors are guaranteed a production slot in the season in each of their three years. These projects are cast from the MFA acting cohort and are fully supported by the department's team of professional designers, stage managers and technicians.

In addition to the practical experience of directing in the season, students will assist faculty and guest directors on department productions, work as a teaching assistant for undergraduate courses, and may pursue independent study projects and internships with our professional theatre partners.

Directors will also have the opportunity to serve as producers of the annual Wagner New Play Festival, a department-wide celebration of new work by our graduate playwrights. In the Festival, each director will be paired with a playwright and will direct a workshop production of a new play.

At the conclusion of their third year, students will present their work in a showcase for industry professionals in Los Angeles and New York.

A non-refundable fee is required to submit the application. Please review the Graduate Division's website for Admissions requirements and information before applying.

   - Statement of Purpose: The Statement of Purpose should not be a reiteration of your C.V. or resume. It is a one-to-two-page essay that describes your past training and experience, your current artistic interests and focus, your reasons for applying to our MFA program, your long-term goals and what makes you a good candidate for our program.
   - Resume or C.V.

Please upload the writing sample as a PDF in the 'Playwriting Writing Sample' section of the online application.
Description:
The MFA playwriting program at UC San Diego is a three-year, intensive writing program. We only admit one or two writers a year. The small class size allows us to provide each writer with the individual attention his/her/their work requires. The program is committed to the idea that the theatre is a writer's medium and that the most exciting and vital theatre is created by artists who are passionate, disciplined and engaged in the world-at-large. Students write a full-length play each quarter. Each of these plays has at least a staged reading and some are given a workshop production. Every student will receive at least one production in the Wagner New Play Festival in the third year. All students are eligible to be chosen to receive a mainstage production in the department's subscription season.

The first year focuses on the fundamentals of dramatic writing through weekly writing assignments and the reading of a wide range of plays from the Greeks to the present day. The second year focuses on developing and deepening the writer’s voice and vision. In addition to playwriting workshops, seminars are offered in such subjects as theory and criticism, classical and contemporary drama, screenwriting and television writing, and teaching playwriting. Second- and third-year writers mentor undergraduate playwriting students. All playwriting students meet as a group once a week with the head of playwriting to discuss their work and other subjects of interest.

The UC San Diego Stage Management program is a three year, residency-based program designed to provide a select group of students with the opportunity to acquire the skills and training needed to become a leader in the theatre. It is a rigorous and comprehensive curriculum that combines classroom instruction with a strong emphasis on production work.

In the first year of training, students learn the fundamentals of stage management and serve as an assistant stage manager on at least two productions.

The second year focuses on honing the stage management skills of calling a show, managing a rehearsal room and functioning as the hub of communication. The second-year student will stage manage at least two productions.

ProgramName: PhD in Drama and Theatre with a Specialization in Critical Gender Studies (Joint with UC Irvine)
Description: The joint PhD program in Drama and Theatre between UC San Diego and UC Irvine offers students a unique course of study that combines the scholarly and pedagogical resources of two internationally-recognized departments and faculties. The program admits a small number of students each year for a curriculum that is designed to be completed in five years of residency. Students are typically admitted to and affiliated with a home campus, either UC San Diego or UC Irvine, and during their coursework they are in residence for one year at the other UC campus. During this year of residency, they take seminars, work with faculty and are fully integrated into the life of the other department. Courses on both campuses are available to all students in the program throughout their residency. The program is interdisciplinary in its orientation and it encourages students to develop a course of study that integrates the critical, historical, and theoretical dimensions of theatre and performance studies. The Department of Theatre and Dance is a participating department in the graduate specialization in Critical Gender Studies. The specialization provides specialized training in gender, sexuality, and queer studies for students currently enrolled in a UC San Diego doctoral program. The specialization is designed to complement students’ disciplinary training, introduce them to the central questions and methodologies of CGS as an interdisciplinary field, and provide a credential that will be legible to future employers. Admitted students are required to complete five courses (two core courses and three electives) and to include a chapter on a CGS-related topic in their doctoral dissertation. Upon successful completion of all requirements, students will receive a certificate of completion and the following notation on their transcript: 'Specialization in Critical Gender Studies.'

Description: The graduate program in History at UC San Diego is a vibrant intellectual community of faculty and students who share a commitment to historical research and analysis. Our distinguished faculty train graduate students to become scholars and teachers of the highest caliber. We offer programs of study leading to the Master of Arts (MA) and Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees. Our areas of expertise include the history of the United States, Europe, Latin America, East Asia, the ancient Near East, the Middle East, and Science, Technology, and Medicine. The Department of History does not have a terminal M.A. program. The Master of Arts degree is awarded under one of three circumstances: 1. A student may be awarded a terminal master's degree in lieu of the PhD after successful completion of all requirements for the PhD except for the dissertation. 3. A terminal MA may be granted to students in the PhD program who for various reasons are not able to complete the doctoral degree.

Description: The Master of Arts in Latin American Studies is an interdisciplinary program designed to provide a broad-based, integrated understanding of contemporary Latin America. The program offers both a terminal M.A. degree for students who wish to pursue careers in the private or public sector, and a comprehensive M.A. for those who wish to continue their studies at the doctoral level. The program provides students with the intellectual tools for understanding the region, its people, and its cultures, as well as the challenges facing its societies. In the core curriculum, students study historical and contemporary issues facing Latin America from the perspectives of several different disciplines. They then select a disciplinary concentration (Anthropology, Communication, History, Literature, Political Science, Sociology) and a thematic focus (Cultural Studies, Gender Studies, International Migration, Public Health, or U.S.-Mexico Relations). Students may elect to pursue either Plan I (Thesis) or Plan II (Comprehensive Examination). Both are two-year programs. To earn the M.A. degree, students must demonstrate proficiency in Spanish or Portuguese, and complete a minimum of twelve courses (48 units). Description: The graduate program in linguistics at UC San Diego is a research-oriented program leading to the PhD degree. The department has a strong focus on theoretical linguistics, in the domains of syntax, semantics, phonology, and phonetics. The approach to linguistics is interdisciplinary, with an emphasis on the empirical foundations of linguistic theory. The department has a long-standing tradition of research in a wide variety of languages. Laboratory research is a key component of the doctoral program, with experimental work in phonetics, phonology, syntax, semantics, and language acquisition conducted in the department’s various labs. Students also have the option to pursue research on the linguistic structure of signed languages and on the neural bases of language. Close instructional and research connections exist with the Department of Cognitive Science, the Department of Communication, the Center for Research in Language, the Institute for Neural Computation, and the Salk Institute for Biological Studies. The interdisciplinary nature of research in linguistics is also supported by joint appointments of some Linguistics faculty in other departments, as well as through coursework and research opportunities in allied disciplines.

Description: The Literature Department at UC San Diego has from its beginning been committed to the study of literature and culture in a broad comparative and theoretical frame. Our graduate program is unique in its emphasis on historical and critical thinking and its attention to a wide range of languages and literatures. We do not have separate departments of English, Spanish, French, etc. Instead, our faculty is organized into language sections that include Chinese, English, French, German, Greek, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Latin, Russian, and Spanish. Our graduate students are also admitted into a language section where they are expected to do a substantial portion of their work. At the same time, we have a common curriculum for all students and faculty that is designed to train them as comparatists with a strong theoretical and historical grounding. Our focus on literary study is complemented by a rich and varied engagement with philosophy, history, and social and political thought, as well as with film and media studies, gender studies, and ethnic studies. This combination of linguistic rigor, comparative breadth, and theoretical sophistication has given our program a distinctive cast and a leading place in the country.

MATS has strong interdisciplinary research collaborations, and has particular strengths in the following research thrusts: Advanced Structural Materials; Electronic and Photonic Materials; Energy Materials; Biomaterials and Soft Materials; and Computational Materials Science.

Description: The graduate program in mathematics at UC San Diego has, in its fifty year history, become a large and highly respected department. This is due to the high quality of the faculty and the students. The department has an international reputation for its work in a number of areas of both pure and applied mathematics. The department's graduate students are an important factor in its research life. Students are encouraged to become involved in research at an early stage. There are approximately one hundred fifty graduate students, and the small size of the advanced classes allows for a great deal of interaction between students and faculty. Students who perform well may be offered a teaching assistantship that provides a stipend and pays tuition and fees. Students from underrepresented groups who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents may be eligible for a San Diego fellowship. The department offers a terminal M.A. program with a specialization in statistics. Students in the M.A. program complete a set of qualifying exams for the Ph.D. program and then follow a course of study which enables them to write a thesis (Plan I) or take a comprehensive examination (Plan II). The M.A. programs prepare students for careers in government and industry, for teaching at the community college level, and for further study at the doctoral level in pure or applied mathematics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Requirements: Statement of Purpose is required. 3 letters of recommendation required. Resume or C.V. is recommended. GRE General: Not required. GRE Subject: The Mathematics Subject Test is recommended but not required.
Description: The M.S. in Mathematics is designed to be completed in one year, though students may take up to two years to complete their degree. The M.S. degree is offered in three specializations: Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, and Statistics. We offer two plans for the M.S. degree: Plan I (Thesis) and Plan II (Comprehensive Exam). All students are admitted into Plan II. Students who wish to switch to Plan I must find a thesis advisor and submit a Plan I request form by the end of their first quarter. Plan I is only recommended for students who plan to continue with a Ph.D. degree.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Requirements: A complete application includes the following required materials: Online Application and Fee, Three Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, Statement of Purpose, Resume or C.V., GRE General Test (Optional for Fall 2025 Admissions), GRE Subject Test in Mathematics (Optional for Fall 2025 Admissions), TOEFL or IELTS (if applicable).
Description: The graduate program in mathematics at UC San Diego has been ranked 19th among public universities and 34th overall among U.S. universities by U.S. News & World Report. The department faculty includes many pre-eminent mathematicians who have been recognized for their research by professional societies, prestigious fellowships, and other honors. The graduate program provides a rich and rewarding experience in a beautiful Southern California setting. With five required first-year courses in algebra, analysis, and topology, the program ensures students have a strong, broad foundation in mathematics. The remaining curriculum is flexible and can be tailored for each student's interests and goals. Students are encouraged to attend a variety of research seminars, starting in their first year. After passing the qualifying exams (typically in the second year), students begin to work closely with a faculty advisor. The department has active research groups in most areas of mathematics, including algebra, analysis, combinatorics, geometry, logic, number theory, numerical analysis, probability, and statistics.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Graduate Student Researcher (GSR) appointments, Teaching Assistant (TA) appointments

ProgramName: Master of Science in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: The MAE Department offers three graduate degree programs: the Master of Science (M.S.), the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.), and a new M.S. in Medical Device Engineering. All applicants for graduate admission must hold a Bachelor's degree or the equivalent from a university of recognized standing. A scholastic average of B (3.0 on a 4.0 scale) or better is required for course work completed in upper-division or prior graduate study. Applicants who already hold a Ph.D. degree will not be admitted into the Ph.D. program. In addition, applicants who already hold a M.S. degree in a particular discipline will not be admitted into the same M.S. program at UC San Diego.
