Description: The M.S. degree program is intended to provide students with an opportunity to strengthen their knowledge and competence in a particular area of mechanical and aerospace engineering and to develop experience in performing engineering research. The program is for qualified students who have a bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or a related field. There are two plans of study available, one with a thesis and one without. The M.S. program should be considered a preparatory step for students who wish to pursue a Ph.D. degree at UC San Diego, as the Ph.D. program requires a master’s degree for admission. Full time M.S. students are expected to complete their degree requirements by the end of their second year.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

ProgramName: PhD in Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering
Requirements: The MAE Department requires all applicants to have a bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in engineering, mathematics, or physics. Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale from their bachelor's granting institution.

Description: The MAE Ph.D. program is intended to prepare students for a career in research and/or academia. A key element of the Ph.D. program is the conduct of independent research under the supervision of a faculty advisor, culminating in the preparation and defense of a doctoral dissertation. We offer a wide range of cutting-edge research opportunities that span the breadth of modern mechanical and aerospace engineering. Our graduate students come from the best universities in the U.S. and around the world, and go on to become leaders in academia, industry and government.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Requirements: Applications are submitted through the American Medical College Application Service (AMCAS). All applicants must take the Medical College Admission Test (MCAT). A minimum of three letters of recommendation are required (maximum of five), submitted through the AMCAS Letter Service. Required coursework includes one year of Biology with lab, one year of General Chemistry with lab, one year of Organic Chemistry with lab, one course in Biochemistry, and one year of Physics. AP scores are accepted to satisfy requirements if they are documented on your undergraduate transcript.
Description: The UC San Diego School of Medicine MD degree program is a four-year program that provides comprehensive education in the art and science of medicine. Our curriculum is designed to prepare students for a career in any field of medicine, with a strong emphasis on primary care and the needs of underserved communities. The program is divided into two phases: the pre-clerkship phase and the clerkship phase. In the pre-clerkship phase, students learn the foundational sciences of medicine, including anatomy, biochemistry, and physiology. In the clerkship phase, students rotate through various clinical specialties, such as internal medicine, pediatrics, and surgery.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
Accredidation: The University of California, San Diego School of Medicine is a fully accredited medical school. Our last accreditation site visit was in March 2022. We were granted continued full accreditation for an eight-year term by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME).

Description: The graduate program in music at UC San Diego offers the degrees of Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) and Master of Arts (M.A.). The program is highly selective. It is not our goal to produce a large number of graduates but to provide an environment in which a few gifted individuals can pursue their musical interests and develop their skills to the fullest. We are interested in students who have already demonstrated significant achievement and who are dedicated to a life of continuing artistic and intellectual growth. The M.A. is a two-year degree with concentrations in Composition, Computer Music, or Integrative Studies. The M.A. program is designed for students who have not yet had sufficient background and training to be admitted to the Ph.D. program. The M.A. is also appropriate for those who wish to pursue a more limited course of study beyond the bachelor’s degree. Students are admitted to one of the three areas of concentration listed above.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowships, Teaching Assistantships, Graduate Student Researcher Assistantships

More information can be found at this link. GRE: Not Required for Fall 2024 admissions.
Description: The Doctor of Musical Arts (DMA) in Contemporary Music Performance is offered by the Department of Music at UC San Diego. The program is unique in that it is a research-oriented doctoral program in performance, designed to be on a par with the Ph.D. The program aims to produce performers who are also scholars and scholar-performers who are also outstanding musicians. The program is intentionally small to allow for intensive contact between students and faculty. The department has a large and varied faculty in performance who work in a variety of musical styles with emphasis in contemporary music. Most performance faculty perform in the top professional new music ensembles in the San Diego area, including the San Diego Symphony, or are active as soloists and chamber musicians nationally and internationally. The program gives students a strong technical foundation on their instrument, experience in a wide range of repertoire, and the development of a personal artistic vision through in-depth study of music of the 20th and 21st centuries. Students will gain experience in a variety of performance situations, from solo and chamber music to large ensemble, and will be given opportunities to work with composers and to participate in the creation of new works. Students will have access to a wide variety of courses in the Department of Music, including courses in composition, computer music, and integrative studies.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Requirements: In addition to the general application, the following materials are required to be submitted in support of the application to the Ph.D. in Music Program: Letters of Recommendation (3 required), Statement of Purpose, Resume or CV, Writing Samples (Two writing samples, at least one of which must be analytical or scholarly in nature), Portfolio, and English Language Proficiency (for international applicants).
Concentration: Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, Performance
Description: The Ph.D. program in Music is an integrated degree with five specialized areas of study, referred to as 'research areas': Composition, Computer Music, Integrative Studies, and Performance. It is a fundamental feature of the Department that these research areas are not separate departments, but interact on a daily basis. The focus of the program is on the creation of new music and the development of new ideas about music. Music at UCSD is understood to be an art of sound, and all sound is considered potential material for musical creation and inquiry. We do not privilege any one style or tradition of music making or study, and we encourage our graduate students to explore the rich variety of musics available to them. To this end we offer a strong faculty representing a wide array of musical interests. Our goal is to prepare graduate students to be the next generation of composers, performers, and scholars who will lead the field in the twenty-first century.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of tuition and most fees

Requirements: Applicants are asked to submit a statement of purpose that describes their past research experience, their future research interests, and their motivation for pursuing a Ph.D. in neurosciences. We recommend that applicants also identify several faculty members whose research they find particularly interesting. Applicants are asked to provide three letters of recommendation from individuals who are in a position to analyze their academic ability and research potential. These letters should be from faculty and/or supervisors who are familiar with the applicant's research experience. Applicants are asked to submit a resume or curriculum vitae that outlines their academic and research background.
Description: The Neurosciences Graduate Program at UC San Diego is an inter-institutional program dedicated to training the next generation of leaders in neuroscience research, education, and outreach. The program spans more than 30 departments and sections across UC San Diego and three affiliated research institutes: the Salk Institute for Biological Studies, the Sanford Burnham Prebys Medical Discovery Institute, and The Scripps Research Institute. Established in 1968, the program is the oldest and one of the largest neuroscience graduate programs in the country. Our more than 160 faculty provide an extraordinary breadth of research and training opportunities, in a collaborative and collegial atmosphere. Students receive five years of guaranteed financial support and typically complete their PhDs in an average of 5.5 years. The program is committed to a holistic admissions process, recognizing that a diverse and inclusive student body is a cornerstone of a preeminent graduate program.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: Full funding package including tuition, fees, and a stipend of $40,000 (2023-2024 rate).
ScholarshipPercentage: 100% of tuition and fees for all admitted students.

Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences, applicants must be a U.S. Citizen or Permanent Resident. A bachelor's degree is not required for admission, however, applicants must have a cumulative GPA of a 3.0 or above and have completed the required prerequisite courses from a U.S. accredited college or university. All prerequisite courses must be completed with a grade of "C-" or better. The PCAT exam is not required, but optional for Fall 2025 admissions. Three letters of recommendation, with at least one from a science professor, are required.
Department: Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
Description: The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences at UC San Diego offers a four-year Doctor of Pharmacy (Pharm.D.) degree program that is committed to providing an innovative and flexible curriculum in a highly inter-disciplinary environment. The curriculum is taught by a unique blend of faculty from the School of Pharmacy, the UC San Diego School of Medicine and other campus departments. The program focuses on the students' development as future leaders in pharmacy by providing opportunities for inter-professional collaborations in patient care, leadership roles in professional organizations, and specialized elective streams that are tailored to the students' career goals. The small class size, paired with San Diego's collaborative biotech and medical environment, allows for a personalized and team-oriented experience which prepares students to be successful leaders in patient care, research, and industry.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
Accredidation: The University of California San Diego Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences’ Doctor of Pharmacy program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education, 190 South LaSalle Street, Suite 3000, Chicago, IL 60603, 312/664-3575; FAX 866/228-2631, web site www.acpe-accredit.org.

ProgramName: Master of Science in Pharmaceutical Sciences
Department: Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
Description: The Master of Science in Drug Development and Product Management is a one-year, in-person master’s degree program that provides students with a multidisciplinary education to meet the needs of the pharmaceutical industry. The program is specifically designed to provide students with the key knowledge and skills that are essential to transition to a career in drug development and product management. Students will learn the process of how a drug or a product moves from the laboratory to the marketplace from world-renowned faculty at the University of California San Diego. Students will also experience hands-on training via the capstone course where they will learn from and interact with industry leaders in drug development, clinical trials, business development and project management. The curriculum also provides students with the training in professional development to support successful career placement following graduation.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Department: Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences
Description: The Skaggs School of Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Sciences offers a PhD degree program in Pharmaceutical and Biomedical Sciences. The doctoral degree program provides a strong foundation in the fundamental principles of drug discovery, drug delivery and drug action, and prepares students for a variety of careers in academia, the pharmaceutical and biotech industries, as well as government. The curriculum is interdisciplinary, offers training in diverse areas of pharmaceutical and biomedical sciences, and fosters collaborations between students and faculty in different specializations. The Skaggs School of Pharmacy is part of UC San Diego Health Sciences, which also includes the School of Medicine, the Wertheim School of Public Health and Human Longevity Science, and UC San Diego Health. UC San Diego Health Sciences is an innovative, collaborative, and highly translational environment for biomedical research.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: $42,000 annual stipend, plus payment of tuition and fees.

Requirements: Applicants for admission to the MA program should have an undergraduate major in philosophy or an equivalent set of courses in the discipline. The Departmental Admissions Committee will consider exceptions in the case of applicants with unusually strong records in other disciplines and some work in philosophy.
Description: The department offers a terminal M.A. program in philosophy. The M.A. is designed to be completed in one year (three quarters) of full-time study. The program is designed for students who can benefit from a year of graduate-level work in philosophy. Some students enter the program to deepen their knowledge of philosophy before applying to Ph.D. programs, while others are interested in the connections between philosophy and their undergraduate major or profession. Still others are drawn to the program out of an interest in philosophy and a desire to pursue it at a more advanced level. The M.A. program has been very successful at preparing students for admission to Ph.D. programs in philosophy. In recent years, our M.A. students have been admitted with multi-year funding packages to Ph.D. programs at Brown University, Columbia University, Cornell University, the University of Michigan, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, Princeton University, the University of Southern California, Stanford University, the University of Texas at Austin, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, among many others. The M.A. program draws on the same faculty and graduate seminars as our Ph.D. program, and M.A. students are integrated into the regular life of the department.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Requirements: Applicants are required to submit an online application which includes: transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, three letters of recommendation, a Statement of Purpose, and a writing sample. The Statement of Purpose should describe your scholarly and research interests, and your reasons for wanting to pursue a Ph.D. in Philosophy at UC San Diego (maximum of 2 single-spaced pages). The Writing Sample should be one sample of your philosophical writing (a single paper of no more than 25 double-spaced pages). For the Fall 2024 admissions cycle, GRE scores are not required and will not be accepted. International applicants must demonstrate English language proficiency.
Description: The graduate program in philosophy at UC San-Diego is a Ph.D. program. The department offers a broad range of courses, a distinguished and dedicated faculty, a diverse and excellent group of graduate students, and a supportive intellectual environment in which to pursue graduate work. The program is designed to be completed in five years. The curriculum is flexible, designed to allow students to develop their own interests, while at the same time insuring that they receive a solid grounding in the core areas of philosophy.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipType: Fellowship and employment as a Teaching Assistant

Requirements: The Department of Physics requires a minimum of a bachelor's degree in physics or a related discipline from an accredited university. A minimum GPA of 3.0 on a 4.0 scale is required. Applicants should have a strong background in undergraduate physics, including courses in mechanics, electricity and magnetism, quantum mechanics, and thermodynamics. Research experience is highly recommended.
Description: The Department of Physics offers a terminal M.S. program for students wishing to obtain a master's degree before pursuing a career in industry, business, education, or government. The program consists of a minimum of 36 units, which must include at least 24 units of graduate-level physics coursework. The program is designed to be completed in one to two academic years. The M.S. is a Plan II (comprehensive exam) degree. The comprehensive exam consists of the General Physics Exam, which is offered once a year at the start of the fall quarter. Incoming M.S. students have two opportunities to pass the General Physics Exam. Required Courses: Must pass five courses, each with a grade of B- or better from: PHYS 200A, PHYS 200B, PHYS 201, PHYS 210A, PHYS 212A. Elective Courses: Must pass at least three elective graduate courses in physics, each with a grade of B- or better.

At the same time, students are encouraged to get involved in research within the first year by participating in research projects with our faculty. After passing a qualifying exam based on core graduate course material, students focus on their Ph.D. research. All of our Ph.D. students are supported as teaching assistants or research assistants during their graduate career. The Ph.D. degree is granted in recognition of the candidate's demonstrated ability to carry out independent and original research in his or her chosen field.

The statement of purpose should be a concise, well-written essay about your background and why you are pursuing a graduate degree in political science. A Resume or CV is required. A writing sample is required. This may be a paper written for a course, a chapter of an honors thesis, or a similar piece of scholarly work that demonstrates your ability to conduct research and write a professional-level paper. There is no specified page length, but we recommend sending your best work. Please upload your writing sample in the online application. The GRE is not required for Fall 2024 admissions.
Description: The standalone M.A. Program offers a comprehensive, one-year course of study in Political Science. Students take ten courses, including courses in three of the four primary fields of the discipline (American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, and Political Theory). They write a significant research paper as their capstone experience. The program provides the intellectual and analytic tools for a professional career in public service, government, or the private sector. It can also serve as a foundation for further graduate study at the Ph.D. level.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

Description: The graduate program in Political Science at the University of California San Diego is a top-ranked program that provides doctoral students with the theoretical and methodological skills to conduct high-quality, cutting-edge research. The Department of Political Science offers the Ph.D. in four primary fields of study: American Politics, Comparative Politics, International Relations, and Political Theory. We also offer a secondary concentration in Methodology. Our students work closely with world-renowned faculty who are leading scholars in their fields. The program is designed to prepare students for careers in academia, research, and public service.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html

ProgramName: PhD in Political Science and International Affairs
Requirements: Submit the UC San Diego Application for Graduate Admission online. The following materials should be submitted with your application: Statement of Purpose, Resume or C.V., Three Letters of Recommendation, Transcripts, GRE General Test, English Language Proficiency, Writing Sample.

Description: The joint Ph.D. in Political Science and International Affairs is a collaboration between the Department of Political Science in the School of Social Sciences and the School of Global Policy and Strategy (GPS). It is designed to join the department’s expertise in political science research with GPS's regional and multidisciplinary expertise. Students in the joint program pursue a Ph.D. in political science with a special emphasis in international affairs. All students in the program take the political science courses required for a Ph.D. in political science. Students also complete a set of core courses at GPS in international relations, policy analysis, finance and management, and quantitative methods. Joint program students must have a regional concentration. Available regions are Latin America, Southeast Asia, Northeast Asia, and China. Students take at least four courses in their regional concentration area. The dissertation for a student in the joint program must be on a topic in international affairs.
ProgramWebsiteURL: https://grad.ucsd.edu/admissions/programs.html
ScholarshipAmount: The department offers a five-year funding package to all admitted students. The package includes a stipend (the 2023-2024 academic year stipend was $23,760), and full payment of tuition and fees.

Description: The Master of Public Health (MPH) is a professional degree that provides a population-based perspective and is designed to prepare students to investigate and manage public health problems. The MPH program provides grounding in the foundational public health knowledge, in addition to concentration-specific knowledge, that will enable them to apply public health principles to a variety of settings. Students learn about the social and behavioral sciences, epidemiology, biostatistics, environmental health, and health services administration as well as their application to public health problems. Through a combination of coursework, a hands-on applied practical experience, and a capstone project, students learn to apply public health principles to real-world problems. MPH graduates go on to careers in a wide range of fields in both the public and private sectors.

This unique doctoral program, also known as the Joint Doctoral Program (JDP) in Public Health, provides rigorous training for future leaders in public health. Description: The M.S. in Sociology is a new graduate program at UCSD designed to provide students with a strong foundation in sociological theory, research methods, and a chosen substantive area of study. The M.S. degree is earned with the completion of 40 units of coursework, a major paper, and a comprehensive exam. It is a one-year program with courses that introduce students to the key ideas and debates in sociology and provide them with the skills to conduct their own research. Students will have the opportunity to work closely with faculty members who are leaders in their fields, and to develop their own research interests. The program is ideal for students who want to pursue a career in research, policy, or the non-profit sector, as well as for those who want to continue on to a Ph.D. program in sociology or a related field.

Description: The graduate program in Sociology at UCSD offers a PhD in Sociology. The faculty has a collective expertise in a broad range of sociological theory from classical to contemporary, and we offer rigorous training in both quantitative and qualitative methods. In addition to general theory and methods, the program provides specialized training in eight areas of specialization: Comparative-Historical Sociology; Inequality and Social Stratification; Political Sociology and Social Movements; Sociology of Culture; Sociology of Education; Sociology of Law; Sociology of Migration; and Science, Technology and Medicine.

Description: Classical studies is the interdisciplinary study of the civilizations of ancient Greece and Rome. Its subject matter is the entire public and private life of these peoples, and its evidence is everything they made or wrote. The curriculum of the program therefore comprises archaeology, art, drama, history, law, literature, mythology, philosophy, political theory, religion, and science. Each of the participating departments—History, Literature, Philosophy, Political Science, Theatre and Dance, and Visual Arts—offers courses in its own discipline, but the Classical Studies Program is the only academic unit on campus that fosters and supports the integrated study of the ancient world. Students are urged to combine courses in the core disciplines of history, literature, and philosophy with relevant courses in the other departments to produce a minor that is both broad and deep.

Description: The climate change studies (CCS) minor provides students with a broad, interdisciplinary background in the science, policy, and social issues of climate change. The minor is a supplement to any major at UC San Diego. It is appropriate for students with a wide range of career and life interests, from science and engineering to the social sciences and humanities. A major goal of the minor is to foster an interdisciplinary understanding among students from a variety of backgrounds and interests. Through this program, students will learn the scientific basis of climate change, the impacts of climate change on society and ecosystems, and the legal, economic, and policy frameworks for addressing climate change. The minor will culminate in a capstone experience through which students will engage in a climate change-related project that has both an academic and experiential component. Students who complete the minor will have a unique, well-rounded perspective on climate change that will serve them in their future careers and as engaged and informed citizens.

The critical gender studies major offers students a unique opportunity to study gender and sexuality from a wide variety of perspectives in the humanities, social sciences, and sciences. The program’s curriculum emphasizes the study of gender and sexuality as it intersects with other categories of analysis, including race, class, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability. Description: The global health major is a bachelor of arts degree and is designed to provide students an understanding of the complex determinants of health and disease in a global context. Students graduating with a global health major will develop skills in qualitative and quantitative research and communication and will gain in-depth knowledge of a particular global health topic through an upper-division concentration. The capstone of the major is a senior thesis or project that will allow students to integrate and apply the knowledge and skills they have gained in the major. Description: Linguistics is the scientific study of language, the most complex and uniquely human of our cognitive abilities. Students also have the opportunity to study a wide range of languages. The department has two majors, each offering the BA or BS degree. The linguistics major provides a foundation in theoretical linguistics. The language studies major emphasizes proficiency in one or more languages, combined with a basic knowledge of linguistic principles. The department is a part of the Division of Social Sciences, but the study of linguistics also interacts with and draws from disciplines in the Division of Arts and Humanities and the Division of Biological Sciences, and the Jacobs School of Engineering. Students can complete a general linguistics major or specialize in a particular area. This specialization is intended for majors who are interested in the psychological and biological aspects of language. It is a good option for students interested in careers in speech pathology and audiology or in marketing, and for students who are considering graduate study in cognitive science, psychology, or a related field.

Description: The speculative design major trains students in a human-centered and technically rigorous design process. Through their studio practice and in concert with lecture and seminar courses, students in speculative design learn the theories and histories that underpin design practice as well as how to conduct research to understand the needs of the communities they are designing for and the potential impacts of their work. The speculative design major prepares students to be versatile and adaptable members of an ever-changing design field, with strong technical skills and a critical understanding of the role design plays in society. Students will develop skills in collaboration, critique, and communication, ready to engage with and lead design teams. The major prepares students to enter a wide variety of design careers, such as product and interaction design (UX/UI), design research and strategy, and creative technology. Students in the speculative design major will be able to demonstrate their design abilities by producing a professional-level portfolio of design projects, and to demonstrate their design knowledge by completing a series of rigorous studio and seminar courses. Students in the program will be able to produce designs that demonstrate an understanding of design principles, critical thinking, and technical skills in a variety of media, as well as working independently and in collaborative groups.
